question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z<1.08).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.1\,$ | $\,0.1230\,$ | $\,0.1210\,$ | $\,0.1192\,$ |
| $\,-1.0\,$ | $\,0.1446\,$ | $\,0.1423\,$ | $\,0.1401\,$ |
| $\,-0.9\,$ | $\,0.1685\,$ | $\,0.1660\,$ | $\,0.1635\,$ |

$P(Z<1.08)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/eeab34aacca66478c43609c77d4b3b80a48660c761c025a8c36b4bc55b4e46f8.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1)$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>-a)=P(Z<a)=Φ(a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z<1.08).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/ab1866c1c59d84c7024fa5d8a2d03b0eb13605e15dc630073713c06119c5fca6.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z>-1.08).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/07b34256562ab727d4f4ed7ef29d077483bf30b6195ca522a55c5577fd947ed7.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z<1.08) & =P(Z>-1.08) \\  & =1-P(Z<-1.08) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.08) \\  & =1-0.1401 \\  & =0.8599.\end{aligned}
$$
